"""Block parsing boundary for the CommonMark pipeline."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
import re
from .fenced_code import parse_fenced_code
from .html_blocks import parse_html_block
from .indented_code import parse_indented_code
from .references import extract_definitions


@dataclass
class Block:
    """A minimal block node retaining source for later inline parsing."""

    kind: str
    children: list["Block"] = field(default_factory=list)
    literal: str = ""
    level: int | None = None
    info: str = ""


@dataclass
class Document:
    """Ordered block tree and document-wide reference definitions."""

    children: list[Block] = field(default_factory=list)
    references: dict[str, object] = field(default_factory=dict)


def _thematic(line: str) -> bool:
    match = re.fullmatch(r" {0,3}([*_\-])(?:[ \t]*\1){2,}[ \t]*", line)
    return bool(match)


def _atx(line: str):
    match = re.match(r"^ {0,3}(#{1,6})(?:[ \t]+(.*)|[ \t]*$)", line)
    if not match:
        return None
    content = (match.group(2) or "").strip(" \t")
    content = re.sub(r"[ \t]+#+[ \t]*$", "", content).strip(" \t")
    return len(match.group(1)), content


def parse_blocks(markdown: str) -> Document:
    """Parse supported block structures, retaining inline source where needed."""
    document = Document()
    paragraph: list[str] = []

    def finish_paragraph() -> None:
        if not paragraph:
            return
        # Continuation indentation is structural, while trailing whitespace on
        # those lines remains available to the inline parser (for hard breaks).
        lines = [paragraph[0].lstrip(" \t")]
        lines.extend(line.lstrip(" \t") for line in paragraph[1:])
        literal = "\n".join(lines).rstrip(" \t")
        literal = extract_definitions(literal + "\n", document.references).rstrip("\n")
        if literal:
            document.children.append(Block(kind="paragraph", literal=literal))
        paragraph.clear()

    lines = markdown.splitlines()
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        if not line.strip(" \t"):
            finish_paragraph()
            i += 1
            continue
        fenced = parse_fenced_code(lines[i:])
        html = parse_html_block(lines[i:], paragraph_open=bool(paragraph))
        heading = _atx(line)
        if fenced:
            finish_paragraph()
            content, info, consumed = fenced
            document.children.append(Block(kind="fenced_code", literal=content, info=info))
            i += consumed
        elif _thematic(line):
            finish_paragraph()
            document.children.append(Block(kind="thematic_break"))
            i += 1
        elif heading:
            finish_paragraph()
            level, content = heading
            document.children.append(Block(kind="heading", level=level, literal=content))
            i += 1
        elif html:
            finish_paragraph()
            raw, consumed = html
            document.children.append(Block(kind="html_block", literal=raw))
            i += consumed
        else:
            code = parse_indented_code(lines[i:], paragraph_open=bool(paragraph))
            if code:
                finish_paragraph()
                content, consumed = code
                document.children.append(Block(kind="indented_code", literal=content))
                i += consumed
            else:
                paragraph.append(line)
                i += 1
    finish_paragraph()
    return document
"""Fenced code block recognition."""

import re

_OPEN = re.compile(r"^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$")


def parse_fenced_code(lines: list[str]):
    if not lines:
        return None
    match = _OPEN.match(lines[0])
    if not match:
        return None
    fence, info = match.groups()
    if fence[0] == "`" and "`" in info:
        return None
    info = info.strip(" \t")
    indent = len(lines[0]) - len(lines[0].lstrip(" "))
    close = re.compile(r"^ {0,3}" + re.escape(fence[0]) + r"{" + str(len(fence)) + r",}[ \t]*$")
    content = []
    for index, line in enumerate(lines[1:], 1):
        if close.match(line):
            return "".join(line[max(indent, 0):] + "\n" for line in content), info, index + 1
        content.append(line)
    return "".join(line[indent:] + "\n" for line in content), info, len(lines)
"""CommonMark parser integration interfaces."""

from .blocks import Document, parse_blocks
from .inlines import parse_inlines


def render(markdown: str) -> str:
    """Render a complete Markdown document to HTML.

    This foundation exposes the integration point; parsing and rendering behavior
    are supplied by later parser capabilities.
    """
    document = parse_blocks(markdown)
    for block in document.children:
        if block.kind in {"paragraph", "heading"}:
            parse_inlines(block.literal, document.references)
    return ""


__all__ = ["Document", "parse_blocks", "parse_inlines", "render"]
from commonmark_parser.blocks import parse_blocks


def test_consecutive_lines_form_paragraphs_separated_by_blank_lines():
    first, second, third = "alpha", "beta", "gamma"
    document = parse_blocks(first + "\n" + second + "\n\n" + third + "\n")

    assert len(document.children) == 2
    assert all(node.kind == "paragraph" for node in document.children)
    assert document.children[0].literal.splitlines() == [first, second]
    assert document.children[1].literal.strip() == third


def test_boundary_blanks_are_ignored_and_continuation_indent_is_removed():
    document = parse_blocks("\n  alpha\n    beta\n\n")

    assert len(document.children) == 1
    assert document.children[0].kind == "paragraph"
    assert document.children[0].literal.splitlines() == ["alpha", "beta"]


def test_continuation_trailing_spaces_are_preserved_but_final_trailing_spaces_are_trimmed():
    document = parse_blocks("alpha  \n  beta  \n\n")

    assert document.children[0].literal == "alpha  \nbeta"


def test_whitespace_only_lines_separate_paragraphs():
    document = parse_blocks("one\n \t \ntwo")

    assert [node.literal for node in document.children] == ["one", "two"]


def test_empty_and_blank_only_documents_have_no_paragraphs():
    assert parse_blocks("").children == []
    assert parse_blocks(" \t\n\n").children == []
from commonmark_parser.blocks import parse_blocks
from commonmark_parser.fenced_code import parse_fenced_code
from commonmark_parser.html_blocks import parse_html_block
from commonmark_parser.indented_code import parse_indented_code
from commonmark_parser.references import extract_definitions


def test_thematic_break_interrupts_paragraph_and_rejects_mixed_markers():
    doc = parse_blocks("alpha\n* * *\n* - *\n")
    assert [node.kind for node in doc.children] == ["paragraph", "thematic_break", "paragraph"]


def test_atx_heading_level_closing_markers_and_invalid_opening():
    doc = parse_blocks("### alpha ###\n#gamma\n")
    assert [(n.kind, n.level, n.literal.strip()) for n in doc.children] == [("heading", 3, "alpha"), ("paragraph", None, "#gamma")]


def test_indented_code_preserves_interior_blank_and_extra_indent():
    assert parse_indented_code(["    alpha", "", "      beta", ""]) == ("alpha\n\n  beta\n", 3)


def test_indented_code_does_not_interrupt_paragraph():
    assert parse_indented_code(["    alpha"], paragraph_open=True) is None


def test_fenced_code_requires_matching_closer_and_removes_indent():
    assert parse_fenced_code(["  ~~~ py", "  alpha", "~~~~", "tail"]) == ("alpha\n", "py", 3)
    assert parse_fenced_code(["``` bad ` info"]) is None


def test_html_comment_runs_through_closing_line():
    assert parse_html_block(["<!-- start", "", "finish -->", "tail"]) == ("<!-- start\n\nfinish -->\n", 3)


def test_html_custom_standalone_tag_cannot_interrupt_paragraph():
    assert parse_html_block(["<custom>"], paragraph_open=True) is None
    assert parse_html_block(["<div>", "body", "", "tail"], paragraph_open=True) == ("<div>\nbody\n", 2)


def test_reference_definitions_normalize_and_keep_first():
    refs = {}
    remaining = extract_definitions("[Alpha]: /first\n[alpha]: /second\n", refs)
    assert remaining == ""
    assert refs == {"alpha": ("/first", None)}


def test_block_parser_collects_references_document_wide():
    doc = parse_blocks("[Label]: /target\n\nvisible\n")
    assert doc.references == {"label": ("/target", None)}
    assert [node.literal for node in doc.children] == ["visible"]
